slice.name: Limestone Courtyard House
slice.concept: A single-storey Mediterranean garden house formed as an asymmetric L around a sheltered, planted courtyard garden. A dominant terracotta-tiled roof covers the social heart—open-plan kitchen, dining and living—while lower pitched wings contain three bedrooms and two bathrooms, giving the house a clear hierarchy and calm private circulation. Warm ivory plaster, pale limestone detailing and generous, room-scaled garden glazing create a contemporary but enduring character.
hierarchy: Primary social volume: the broadest and tallest-pitched rectangular bar contains the open-plan kitchen, dining and living spaces, opening directly to the veranda, terrace, pool and sheltered garden.
Private wing: a lower-roofed perpendicular bar forms one side of the L and contains the three-bedroom, two-bathroom suite arrangement with a quiet internal corridor.
Garden edge: the inside of the L is defined by a continuous covered veranda and terrace, making the courtyard the shared outdoor room rather than an exposed rear yard.
Entrance element: a recessed, shaded arrival notch at the outer elbow of the L provides a legible transition into the central living space without adding a detached structure.
slice.roofLanguage: Terracotta clay tile pitched roofs establish a clear main-roof hierarchy: the principal social bar has the broadest, most prominent gabled roof, while the bedroom wing uses a lower, subordinate pitched roof. Deep eaves shade glazing and veranda edges; roof forms remain simple, rectangular and coherent, with no competing roof clutter.
slice.entrance: Approach through restrained planting to a shaded, recessed entrance beneath the lower roof edge at the L-junction. Pale limestone paving and a limestone-framed door surround distinguish the threshold, with a protected pause before entry into the open-plan heart of the house.
slice.outdoorLiving: A covered veranda runs along the inward-facing garden façade of the social volume, sized for dining and relaxed seating. It steps out to a limestone terrace and a modest rectangular swimming pool positioned within the sheltered garden, with direct visual and physical connection to kitchen, dining and living areas. Bedroom glazing is directed toward quieter planted garden margins for privacy.
slice.landscape: Keep the flat site open and composed: a sheltered central garden combines pale gravel, clipped evergreen structure, low aromatic Mediterranean planting and a small number of sculptural trees. Use restrained planting bands to screen bedroom windows and frame the pool terrace, retaining broad clear lawn or gravel margins around the house. No level changes, retaining walls or detached garden structures.

input.brief: Design a single-storey Mediterranean garden house with three bedrooms and two bathrooms on a completely flat 60 by 48 metre site. Compose connected rectangular volumes in an asymmetric L shape around a sheltered garden. Use warm ivory plaster, pale limestone accents, terracotta pitched roofs with a clear main-roof hierarchy, a shaded entrance and generous room-proportioned glazing. Include a modern open-plan kitchen and dining area, comfortable private bedroom circulation, a covered veranda facing the garden, a modest swimming pool, a terrace and restrained planting. Keep the house coherent and fully editable, with no detached buildings, terrain changes or basement.
